question: What does section 60FA of the Employment Act 1955 provide regarding paternity leave?

supporting_quotes.quote: paid paternity leave at his ordinary rate of pay for a period of seven consecutive days in respect of each confinement
restricted to five confinements irrespective of the number of spouses
employed by the same employer at least twelve months immediately before the commencement of such paternity leave

question: Under section 12(2) of the Employment Act 1955, what is the minimum notice period for an employee who has been employed for three years if the contract has no written notice provision, and under section 13(1) can either party end the contract without serving that notice?

supporting_quotes.quote: six weeks’ notice if he has been so employed for two years or more but less than five years on such date
The length of such notice shall be the same for both employer and employee
Either party to a contract of service may terminate such contract of service without notice
by paying to the other party an indemnity of a sum equal to the amount of wages which would have accrued to the employee during the term of such notice

notes: Converted from single to multi (same Act) for the 58-question design; s.13 added as second gold section.

question: Under section 60D of the Employment Act 1955, which five gazetted public holidays must be included in an employee's eleven paid public holidays?

supporting_quotes.quote: on eleven of the gazetted public holidays, five of which shall be

(i) the National Day; (ii) the Birthday of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong; (iii) the Birthday of the Ruler or the Yang di-Pertua Negeri, as the case may be, of the State in which the employee wholly or mainly works under his contract of service, or the Federal Territory Day, if the employee wholly or mainly works in the Federal Territory; (iv) the Workers’ Day; and (v) Malaysia Day

notes: s.60D(1)(b) refers to 'section 8 of the Holidays Act 1951' - an external reference that a naive pattern would wrongly map to Act265#8 (gap G-07).

question: Under section 21 of the Employment Act 1955, what must an employer pay when it terminates a contract of service without notice under subsection 13(1), and by when?

supporting_quotes.quote: shall be paid by the employer to the employee not later than the day on which such contract of service is so terminated
an indemnity of a sum equal to the amount of wages which would have accrued to the employee during the term of such notice or during the unexpired term of such notice

notes: s.21 also refers to 'section 24' (plain form), so a 'section N' pattern would expand to Act265#24 but miss Act265#13.

question: Can I ask my employer to pay my salary in cash instead of into my bank account?

question: Is my annual bonus counted as part of my 'wages' under the Employment Act 1955?

question: Under section 14 of the Consumer Protection Act 1999, how large must the print describing a condition of a free offer be?

question: I bought a product with a defect that cannot be repaired. Can I return it and get a cash refund instead of store credit?

question: Is a shop allowed to advertise a product at a special price when it does not actually intend to sell it at that price?

supporting_quotes.quote: No person shall advertise for supply at a specified price goods or services which that person

Only s.13 covers advertising goods at a specified price without intending, or having reasonable grounds, to supply them at that price.

question: If a term in my consumer contract is oppressive, can the Tribunal for Consumer Claims declare it void?

supporting_quotes.quote: A contract or a term of a contract is substantively unfair if the contract or the term of the contract

distractor_reason: s.24A defines 'unfair term', and ss.24C (procedural unfairness), 24F (power to raise unfairness) and 24H (executed contracts) sit in the same Part IIIA and repeat 'unfair' and 'court or the Tribunal' wording. The substantive test ('oppressive') is only in s.24D, and the power to declare a term void is only in s.24G.
